title: Periodic Quarter-Wave Stack for UV Reflection with SWIR Transmission
scientific_hypothesis: A periodic alternating stack of HfO2 and SiO2 quarter-wave layers tuned for the UV reflection band can achieve high reflectance in 300-450 nm while maintaining high transmittance in 1000-1700 nm without requiring thickness grading or non-periodic optimization.
design_principle: Bragg reflection from periodic dielectric stacks creates high reflectance bands centered at the design wavelength. By setting the quarter-wave condition at the UV band center (~375 nm), the stack reflects UV while the SWIR band falls outside the reflection band and transmits through.
proposed_topology: Air | (HfO2 | SiO2) repeated 12 times | Fused Silica substrate
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for each of the 24 layers
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
maximize mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band
minimize layer count while meeting performance targets
manufacturing_considerations: total layer count fixed at 24 (within 30-layer limit)
all layers must be physically realizable thicknesses (10-500 nm range)
HfO2 and SiO2 are standard ion-beam deposition materials
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for multilayer dielectric coatings
Refractive index contrast between HfO2 (~2.0) and SiO2 (~1.45) determines reflection bandwidth
expected_advantages: L01 and L04 demonstrate dichroic coatings using similar periodic approaches
known_risks: Periodic stacks have limited reflection bandwidth; 300-450 nm is 50% bandwidth which may exceed single periodic stack capability
SWIR transmission may suffer from higher-order reflection bands
L27 notes that periodic designs may not reach global optimum
execution_request_english: Design a periodic multilayer dielectric coating on fused silica substrate with air incidence at 0 degrees. The stack consists of 24 layers: alternating HfO2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) layers, starting with HfO2 adjacent to air. Optimize all 24 individual layer thicknesses to maximize transmittance in 1000-1700 nm wavelength band while maximizing reflectance in 300-450 nm wavelength band. Total layer count is exactly 24. Materials are HfO2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) only. Evaluate performance using transfer matrix method across both wavelength bands.
